title: Totals with SUM
summary: Add up a column of monthly sales and check your answer like a pro.

blocks.text: Finance needs the quarter's sales total before the 10:00 review. You will use SUM to add a range of cells instead of typing every number.
The sheet holds January to March sales, in KES thousands (K), for the North and South shoe-store regions. A typed total goes stale the moment someone corrects a month; a SUM formula never does.

items: Objective: total a column with one formula.
You pass the mission at 80% or more in the Assessment.

blocks.text: Adds every value from B2 to B4. The colon means "through", so the formula keeps working if a value changes.
Relative references move with the formula. Copy =SUM(B2:B4) from B5 one column to the right and Excel rewrites it as =SUM(C2:C4), the South column. One pattern, every region.
Tip: select the range with your keyboard using Shift and the arrow keys, then press Enter.
Four short questions check that you can choose the right range. Amounts are in KES thousands (K); type whole numbers.

items: Ranges use a colon: B2:B4 means B2 through B4.
Totals update automatically when a month is corrected, so never type a total by hand.
Relative references shift when you copy a formula, so one pattern totals every column.

blocks.text: Complete every mission in the Excel Masterclass to earn its Certificate. Next: IF and business thresholds.

items.prompt: Monthly sales for a full year sit in B2 to B13. Which formula gives the yearly total?
